Freeze is a timestamp-based indication, not a pixel comparison. Video with a static image may still present new frames.
A moving currentTime does not prove a new frame was presented. Frame evidence uses the rVFC mediaTime the app already has.
Without rVFC, diagnostics can only assess the media clock; an image freeze cannot be confirmed.
Method CPU times are inclusive and nested: do not add them up. Upload/submission time is not GPU completion time.
Composition cache mode, shared follower, hold/edge sections, export and hidden tabs are excluded from the live video freeze detector.
Long observation gaps are logged separately; they are not automatically treated as a stuck decoder. Hardware/software causes cannot be determined.
Texture/cache warnings are only assessed while media is drawable, not seeking and not paused; seek/unready is not proof of GPU failure.
The write counter counts successful assignments on the instrumented sync/tick/live-correction path; it is not the browser's internal seek count.
Close the panel → play 20–30 seconds → stop → download the report. No export needed.
Volume/mute/rate are element controls, not a measurement of speaker output. All videos unmuted does not prove they all have an audio track.
waiting/stalled and buffered are evidence of element state; they are not audio underrun counters and do not prove the cause of quiet audio.
RMS/peak use getFloatTimeDomainData on the analyser the app already has. Diagnostics never create or change the audio path.
The signal only covers nodes connected to the observed bus, before device/OS output. Coverage is logged; sources outside the bus are not measured.
Low levels or a level drop do not automatically mean a bug: music content, source mixes and intentional changes also alter levels.
Signal sampling is at most 4 times/second; short PCM windows and observation gaps can miss brief glitches. No PCM or audio recordings are stored.
Audio disturbance markers from the diagnostics panel are user reports, not automatic detection or the exact onset time.
History is capped by item count and estimated metadata bytes, not actual RAM. Unavailable/null measurements must not be treated as zero.
